summary: Independent combined review of all four changed paths, 273 added lines, 29 deleted lines, complete modified declarations, supplied domain and workflow authorities, twelve criteria, shared constraints, and twelve smell heuristics found no blocking issue. Recorded exact-source automated and production terminal evidence supports the source assessment. No tests were rerun. Submission and completion remain separate phases.

smell_assessment.name: Mysterious Name
smell_assessment.reasoning: queueIdentity, selectQueue, reconcileQueues, and initiativeMemory describe their responsibilities in established domain terms.

smell_assessment.name: Duplicated Code
smell_assessment.reasoning: Small selection declarations and local safety labels do not justify another abstraction. Canonical action eligibility remains in actionChoices.

smell_assessment.name: Feature Envy
smell_assessment.reasoning: The explorer owns the navigation state it changes and delegates domain eligibility and validation to existing authorities.

smell_assessment.name: Data Clumps
smell_assessment.reasoning: Identity/index already form a selection value, while initiative memory is explicitly grouped in navigation state.

smell_assessment.name: Primitive Obsession
smell_assessment.reasoning: The existing Queue union and backend/reference identity are adequate for this bounded state model; no untyped new workflow protocol appears.

smell_assessment.name: Repeated Switches
smell_assessment.reasoning: Existing local screen branches remain appropriate for explorer input/render coordination. No parallel domain transition cascade was added.

smell_assessment.name: Shotgun Surgery
smell_assessment.reasoning: Production changes stay in the explorer. The other three paths provide corresponding modal regression coverage and instructions.

smell_assessment.name: Divergent Change
smell_assessment.reasoning: Navigation memory, history retention, target display, and row reflow all implement the approved queue slice rather than unrelated cleanup.

smell_assessment.name: Speculative Generality
smell_assessment.reasoning: New state and helpers directly serve queue selection, canonical return, and live reconciliation. No unused extension framework appears.

smell_assessment.name: Message Chains
smell_assessment.reasoning: Local target/record access and chronological receipt selection remain explicit; no new multi-object dependency walk requires hiding.

smell_assessment.name: Middle Man
smell_assessment.reasoning: The new helpers own selection persistence, reconciliation, or restoration side effects, not mere forwarding.

smell_assessment.name: Refused Bequest
smell_assessment.reasoning: The change adds no subclass or implementation that rejects an inherited contract.

standards_reconciliation: Read Standards70 from its original canonical artifact through mq with explicit raw/json formats and OKF import. Independently inspected all source packets, deleted-line ledger, changed README, safety authorities, and committed diff. Agree with its no-blocker conclusion and all twelve heuristic judgements. Its queue subheading suggestion remains optional. Both documentation engineering and technical writing perspectives are adequate; no applicable ADR exists. No substantive disagreement.
spec_reconciliation: Read Spec85 from its original canonical artifact through mq with explicit raw/json formats and OKF import. Independently traced every criterion through navigation memory, canonical context resolution, queue predicates, eligibility/activity separation, refresh restrictions, and field rendering. Agree on all twelve PASS judgements. The removed incidental removal-text assertion retains canonical replacement coverage, while the new public-modal test explicitly checks departure explanation. Inspected recorded suite/compiler, native matrix, and parent consumer evidence without rerunning checks. No substantive disagreement; SVG pixel fidelity and separate final acceptance remain limits.
